findings.title: Team admin/owner authorization uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: The permission check `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the user to be both admin and owner, which is almost never true. A team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will be denied. This should use `||` to allow either role. Consequence: legitimate team administrators cannot add guests to team bookings through this endpoint.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requesting user's credentials instead of organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the credentials of the user making the request, not the booking organizer. If the caller is an attendee or a team admin who is not the organizer, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update the external calendar using the wrong credentials, likely failing to update the organizer's calendar and potentially modifying the caller's calendar with an event they do not own. The handler should always use the booking organizer's credentials, matching the identity in `evt.organizer`.

findings.title: Add guests emails ignore user email preferences
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` or `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` from `eventTypeMetadata`, nor any host/attendee email disabled flags. Other email-sending functions in this file respect these settings. As a result, users who have disabled standard booking emails for attendees or hosts will still receive these new-guest notifications, violating their configured preferences.

findings.title: Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: The filter comparing `guest` to existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`) and to blacklist (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`) is case-sensitive, while the blacklist itself is lowercased. This allows adding the same email with different casing as a duplicate attendee and can bypass the blacklist if the input email is not lowercase. The result is duplicate attendees in the booking and possible emails to addresses that should be blocked.

findings.title: No booking status validation before adding guests
findings.body: The handler does not check `booking.status`. It proceeds even if the booking is cancelled, rejected, or in the past. An API caller can add guests to a cancelled booking, which triggers calendar updates and sends emails about an event that no longer exists. The endpoint should reject modifications for non-active bookings (e.g., status must be ACCEPTED or PENDING).

findings.title: Overriding getNodeMailerPayload may omit cancellation links and other base-class content
findings.body: The new `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` class completely overrides `getNodeMailerPayload` without calling `super`. The base `AttendeeScheduledEmail` may include additional payload elements such as cancellation links, additional notes, or attachments. By not inheriting those, existing attendees receiving this notification may lose important information (e.g., the ability to cancel) that would normally be present in a booking email.

findings.title: Using array index as React key causes focus issues after removal
findings.body: The email input list uses `key={index}`. When an item is removed, React may reuse the DOM node for the wrong item because keys are not stable. This can cause input values to be incorrectly associated and focus loss while editing multiple emails. A stable unique identifier (e.g., a generated id) should be used instead of the index.

findings.title: Error toast prepends error code but translation may be incorrect
findings.body: The `onError` handler builds `message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. `t(err.message)` assumes `err.message` is always a valid translation key. If the server returns a raw error message (e.g., from Prisma), `t` will likely return the key unchanged, resulting in a confusing toast that includes an internal code and an untranslated string. The fallback `unable_to_add_guests` is only used when `message` is empty, which is unlikely because the code prefix ensures it is non-empty.
